prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery, by the Jarillo-Herrero group, of correlated insulating and superconducting states in it, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene alone, credited to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. After the full first-round exchange, the scientific chain still looks the cleanest on the shortlist. Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that flat bands appear at a magic twist angle, and in 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle. The consequence is a gate-tunable platform in which interaction strength, band topology and filling can be varied in one clean device, and independent laboratories have reproduced the phases and extended them to other moire systems and to fractional Chern insulators. I do not count the four explicit supporters as evidence; I weighed the chair's question on what would move me to B041, and I found that none of the specific objections raised against B046 concerns whether the discovery is real. Following Eriksson's request, I would have the citation name the Jarillo-Herrero group as the experimental discoverers, which states the allocation honestly within the three-name limit.
statement.case_against: The field is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and twist-angle disorder still limits sample-to-sample comparison. Experimental credit extends beyond the single credited experimentalist: Yuan Cao as first author and the parallel Dean, Yacoby and Young results are outside the names, as is earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Santos and Peres. The strongest rival, B041, has a longer record, an unusually clean two-name attribution and no open interpretive question, and a colleague who gives maturity the decisive weight can reasonably prefer it. I regard the maturity concern as a question of weighting, not a flaw in the evidence, but I do not think it is trivial.

responses.point: Keeps B041 as the preferred configuration and argues that eight years is short next to a clock programme confirmed and surpassed in many laboratories for over a decade, while saying he would not resist B046 if the maturity and first-author points are judged minor.
responses.response: Your conditional is the right way to frame the choice, and I take it as the answer to the chair's first question. The first-author point is a real limit on the citation, not on the discovery, and I would handle it through the wording that credits the Jarillo-Herrero group. On maturity, the test I apply is whether the observed phases are secure, and they are: correlated insulators, superconducting domes and Chern insulators have been measured by many groups with different fabrication routes. I do not think a decade of clock history is a stronger argument for B041, because the lattice clock is a refinement of a line the committee has honoured in 2005 and 2012, whereas twisted bilayer graphene opens a new class of controllable materials. I do concede that B041 has the cleaner attribution, and I would not oppose it if the committee ends up there.

responses.point: Supports B041 on the originality of the magic-wavelength lattice and the 1e-18 record, lists B046 as the first alternative, and in round one pressed me to say whether my ties to superconducting circuits distort my reading of B031 and B018.
responses.response: I accept your balanced account of both candidates, and I agree that the physics of the lattice clock, magic-wavelength trapping and control of blackbody and other shifts, is real physics and not engineering. Where I differ is on what each prize would tell the wider community. A lattice-clock prize would recognise a further order of magnitude on an already recognised path, whereas B046 recognises a prediction confirmed by a measurement that created a field. I also note that you and I now agree to set circuit QED aside this year. In round one I said the Girvin omission and the timing after 2025 made B031 unclean, and you did not need to press that further. I also take your point that B018 is nearer to B038 and the 2012 prize than to anything I can credit cleanly, so I leave it out of my alternatives.

responses.point: Argues that B041 is mature, concretely attributed and distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes because the comb counts cycles while the lattice clock provides a new atomic reference, and that the opening support for B046 shows excitement and not desert.
responses.response: Your distinction between the comb as counter and the lattice clock as the reference is fair, and it narrows my concern about overlap with 2005; the 2012 overlap remains more of a framing question than a scientific one. I do not agree that the support for B046 shows only excitement. Five top-three placements came from members with different specialities, and each of them stated its weaknesses. I also agree with your own statement that B041 is not a certain winner. If the committee judges that maturity and attribution should decide, then your candidate is the right one and I would vote for it without reservation, which is why it is my first alternative.

responses.point: Moved B046 to the top of his configuration after opening with B001, and asks that the citation say the experimental discovery was made by the Jarillo-Herrero group; keeps B001 as an alternative.
responses.response: I adopt your wording suggestion for the citation, since it states the experimental credit plainly without adding a fourth name. I also agree with your account of why the pairing mechanism should not be disqualifying: the prize would honour the prediction and the observation, not a settled microscopic theory. I disagree with your reading that B001 is the better-established achievement on maturity grounds alone, since the three-name limit leaves Metzner and Muller-Hartmann outside the credit, which you identified yourself, and the discovery content is less direct. I would not oppose it as an alternative.

responses.point: Ranked B046 eighth in the opening on grounds of youth, and now keeps dynamical mean-field theory (B001) as a lead, citing thirty years of confirmation, conceptual originality and the Metzner attribution gap.
responses.response: Your attribution gap on B001 is the point I find hardest to resolve, since the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity mapping are separate contributions and the third name does not cover both. I still think maturity is a reason to prefer B001 in a later year, not a reason to pass over a result already reproduced across many groups. I appreciate that you accept experimental drama does not decide a prize, and I do not wish to claim it does either. My own test for B046 is that the phenomenology is secure, and I would ask what new evidence would change that, which you have not offered.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the unsettled pairing mechanism and about eight years of history as sufficient, or wait; this is the main reason a maturity-minded colleague might prefer B041.
Whether crediting the Jarillo-Herrero group in the citation adequately represents Yuan Cao and the Dean, Yacoby and Young results within a three-name limit.
Whether recognising a second achievement alongside B046 could be defended on attribution; no member has proposed a pairing I could support, and I do not propose one.
Whether B041 should be chosen instead if the committee gives the decisive weight to attribution cleanliness and a longer record.
statement.conflict_note: I work in superconducting circuits, circuit and waveguide QED and quantum computing, direct the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, and have Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson; Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. That bears on B031 and, to a lesser degree, B018, so I would step back from any deliberation specifically on those ballots, and I have taken B031 out of my alternatives. My profile records no collaborative or personal link to any credited name on B046, B041 or B032, so no conflict is apparent for my preferred configuration or alternatives.
